chris: Heads up — ran a tail latency sweep on a customer workload and saw a 40% p99 spike when seq_len crosses ~520 on SM86 nodes. Looks like we picked a slower attention kernel for long sequences.
anya: ugh. Which kernel path? the fused-attn fastpath or the fallback matmul? any logs?
chris: Logs from the runtime probe attached below. Kernel pick shows `attention_v2_prefetch` for <512 and `attention_gemm_fallback` for >=512. But the fallback seems to degrade KV cache locality, causing extra memcpy churn.
chris: ```
[probe] gpu_cap=sm86 tensor_cores=1 bf16=1 fp8=0
[session] seq_len=512 path=attention_v2_prefetch latency=3.8ms
[session] seq_len=520 path=attention_gemm_fallback latency=5.3ms
[trace] kvcache_hits=0.83 kvcache_evictions=0.17 memcpy_us=120
``` 
vikram: runtime-bot screenshot shows batch sizes also shifting — when seq>512 we fall back and batching heuristic reduces batch packing (more single-stream batches). Might be our seqlen-based gating invalidates the continuous-batching window.
ethan: can we force the fastpath for 520 in a canary? If the kernel actually handles >512 but we gate it conservatively, we can widen the threshold.
anya: I looked at the kernel capability detector. For some driver/firmware combos it reports `tensor_cores=1` but `sm_features` mask is missing the fp16-prefetch bit, so our autotuner lumps it into conservative picks.
anya: detector snippet: ```
GPU_INFO: vendor=NVIDIA sm=8.6 compute_cap=86.0 features=[TC,BF16] capability_flags=0x41
DETECT: bf16_supported=true fp8_supported=false prefetch_hint=false
``` 
chris: ah — prefetch_hint=false is what forces fallback. But on those machines prefetch actually works; the probe flag false came from a flaky kernel query after a driver update.
chris: runtime-bot: can you re-run hw-probe on the 3 affected hosts and attach the raw capability dump?
runtime-bot: scheduled job 97431: https://ci.redwood.internal/infra/probes/97431 — will post results here when done :robot_face:
vikram: meanwhile, I pushed a small tweak to the seqlen gating to add a soft-fallback: if the fastpath was used recently on that exact gpu-id, allow +64 slack beyond threshold. Makes canaries safer.
ethan: nice. any perf numbers from canary?
chris: quick A/B: canary on 2 hosts, seq=520 p99 down from 5.3ms -> 3.9ms, throughput stable. kvcache evictions dropped 3x.
anya: ok let's: 1) re-run hw-probe and reconcile capability flag bug, 2) roll the soft-slack tweak to canary fleet, 3) create a follow-up to decide whether to widen permanent threshold or fix detector.
chris: +1. I'll file a small postmortem and link kernel autotune logs.
ethan: cc @platform-team — we should check driver packaging to avoid flaky feature queries next release :eyes:
vikram: putting a short task in the runtime board. tl;dr: detector bug flipped prefetch flag -> bad kernel routing -> KV thrash + p99 spike. :warning:
chris: thanks everyone. if runtime-bot posts probe dumps I'll add them to the thread and the perf ticket.
